title: OpenJarvis Component Adapter
goal: Harvest useful OpenJarvis patterns and rebuild them inside Vega/PIG/LIONCOM without granting OpenJarvis durable authority.

components.title: GitHub / Dependabot read-only digest
components.local_target: PIG/LIONCOM read-only PR and dependency digest
components.reason: The live trial proved a useful read-only digest can be produced with existing gh auth without adopting a Jarvis connector.

components.title: Tool surface audit and deny-by-default wrapper
components.source_pattern: Jarvis registry exposes tools, agents, engines and memory backends
components.local_target: Vega/PIG tool-permission matrix and operator gate surface
components.reason: The registry is useful as an inventory pattern; its default code-assistant toolset is too broad for real repos.

components.title: External skill mining and local skill distillation
components.source_pattern: OpenJarvis skill sources from Hermes, OpenClaw and GitHub
components.local_target: Vega skill registry and curated local Codex skills
components.reason: The best durable use is reading external skills as ideas, then writing small local skills under our guardrails.

components.title: Retrieval and memory shadow benchmark
components.reason: Arena results show broad context retrieval improves answers, while Obsidian remains the truth layer.

components.title: Runtime sandbox protocol
components.reason: OpenJarvis runs locally, but setup pulls toolchains and sees local model inventory; runtime use must stay explicitly scoped.

components.title: Write / fix worker
components.source_pattern: Jarvis code-assistant with file and shell tools
components.local_target: None until a better wrapper exists
components.reason: The live write sandbox produced no patch while Vega/Codex fixed the same toy bug immediately.

local_skill.name: openjarvis-capability-adapter
local_skill.purpose: Guide Codex/Vega to harvest OpenJarvis ideas safely and route them through PIG/LIONCOM guardrails.
